content.value_statement: Project memory and task plans can drift when teams update setup files by hand. This skill initializes SSOT memory, preserves Plans.md tasks, and guides safe migration of workflow files.
actual_capabilities: Initializes decisions.md, patterns.md, and optional session-log.md under .claude/memory.
Preserves Plans.md task sections while applying an updated template structure.
Migrates AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and Plans.md with user confirmation and backups.
Summarizes existing workflow files before asking which rules and tasks to keep.
Routes memory, merge, and migration requests to focused subskill documents.
limitations: It is not intended for implementation work, code review, or temporary session notes.
It depends on the referenced templates existing in the target project.
It modifies local project documentation and memory files only after invocation.
Shell examples should be reviewed before use in unusual repository layouts.

use_cases.title: Set up shared project memory
use_cases.description: Create standard decisions and patterns files for a new project without overwriting existing memory.

use_cases.title: Preserve tasks during template updates
use_cases.description: Update Plans.md structure while keeping active, pending, completed, and archived tasks intact.

use_cases.title: Migrate workflow documentation
use_cases.description: Review current AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and Plans.md files, then move them into a newer workflow format.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize memory files
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a repository without memory files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Initialize the project memory SSOT files. Do not overwrite existing files, and report what was created.

prompt_templates.title: Merge Plans.md safely
prompt_templates.scenario: Preserve task state while refreshing the plan format.
prompt_templates.prompt: Merge the current Plans.md into the latest template. Preserve all task sections and create a backup before writing changes.

prompt_templates.title: Review migration readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Check workflow files before changing them.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and Plans.md. Summarize important rules, tasks, and risks before asking for migration approval.

prompt_templates.title: Run an interactive workflow migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced migration with retained project rules.
prompt_templates.prompt: Migrate AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and Plans.md to the new workflow format. Ask which constraints to keep, back up originals, and summarize the diff.

output_examples.output: Created decisions.md and patterns.md because they were missing. Existing session-log.md was left unchanged. Shared and local Git guidance was reported.

output_examples.input: Merge my Plans.md into the new format.
output_examples.output: The merge kept active, pending, completed, and archived tasks. A timestamped backup was created, and marker definitions were refreshed.
The existing rules and task state were summarized first. After approval, the files were backed up and rewritten with preserved project constraints.

best_practices: Review the summary of existing files before approving a migration.
Keep decisions and reusable patterns in shared memory files.
Check the final diff before committing generated workflow changes.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for unrelated code implementation tasks.
Do not overwrite existing memory files without reviewing their content.
Do not treat session logs as shared project documentation by default.

faq.question: What files does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It manages .claude memory files, Plans.md, AGENTS.md, and CLAUDE.md workflow documentation.

faq.question: Does it overwrite existing files?
faq.answer: The instructions prefer checking existing files first, preserving task data, and creating backups during migration.

faq.question: Can it migrate Plans.md without losing tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. The merge flow extracts active, pending, completed, and archived task sections before applying the template.

faq.question: Is this useful with Codex and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: When should I avoid using it?
faq.answer: Avoid it for normal implementation work, code review, one-off notes, or temporary session-only records.

faq.question: Does it require templates?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented flows reference project templates for memory files and workflow documents.
